findings.description: The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so Terraform does not enforce encryption at rest for uploaded customer data. This leaves encryption dependent on service defaults or individual upload requests rather than making it an explicit bucket control.
The financials bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive financial objects can therefore be stored without an explicitly enforced encryption-at-rest policy.
The operations bucket does not configure default server-side encryption, so stored operational data is not protected by an IaC-enforced encryption-at-rest setting.
The data-science bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. Data uploaded to this bucket lacks an explicitly enforced encryption-at-rest control.
No bucket policy denies requests made without TLS. An otherwise authorized client can access the bucket over unencrypted HTTP, exposing customer data in transit.
No bucket policy enforces SecureTransport for the financials bucket. Authorized access could occur over HTTP, allowing financial data to be exposed in transit.
The configuration does not deny non-TLS S3 requests to the operations bucket. This permits authorized clients to use unencrypted transport.
The bucket lacks a policy requiring TLS via the aws:SecureTransport condition, so authorized requests are not prevented from using HTTP.
Although log objects are encrypted at rest, no bucket policy denies non-TLS access to the logs bucket. Authorized reads or writes may use unencrypted HTTP.
